answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by charging every identity a small, refundable stake that is slashed on fraud, so one operator cannot cheaply run a haven of sock-puppet accounts. Honest agents build a reputation delta over time — their earned history is worth more than a fresh clone — while new identities start with near-zero trust and must prove themselves before touching real value. On a long horizon, that cost asymmetry makes sybil farming unprofitable: copying is cheap, but copying credibility is not.
